records.issue_text: Team/org condition with zero member users produces '= ANY($n)' with an empty array parameter because buildTeamAuthorizationCondition doesn't guard on userIdsFromTeam.length === 0
records.rationale: The diff explicitly *does* guard against empty member user arrays in `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`. It only adds the `ANY(...)` clause when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0`: `if (userIdsFromTeam.length > 0) { conditions.push(Prisma.sql\`("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)\`); }`. Therefore it will not produce `= ANY($n)` with an empty array due to missing length check.

records.issue_text: Asymmetric guarding: org path checks userIdsFromOrg.length > 0 but teamIds.length > 0 is not guarded, showing the empty-team case wasn't considered
records.rationale: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the code always seeds `conditions` with `Prisma.sql\`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)\`` even when `teamIds` could be `[]` (teamsFromOrg may be empty). In contrast, the userId branch is explicitly guarded with `if (userIdsFromOrg.length > 0)`. This asymmetric handling suggests the empty-teamIds case wasn’t explicitly addressed, and depending on how Prisma parameterizes `ANY(${[]})`, it could at least be an untested/unclear edge case (even if it often just evaluates to false).

records.issue_text: Integration tests use single-element arrays (ANY(${[testData.user.id]})) which don't exercise multi-element array typing, so passing tests don't verify the array parameter behavior; should assert emitted SQL (.sql/.values) with arrays of length > 1
records.rationale: The finding claims tests only use single-element arrays and therefore don’t exercise multi-element array behavior, but the diff shows integration tests asserting `ANY(${[...]})` with multiple elements, e.g. `Prisma.sql` with `("teamId" = ANY(${[ testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id ]}))` and `("userId" = ANY(${[ testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id ]}))`, which does exercise multi-element array parameterization.
